1.s: A great hymn of praise: God chose us in Christ before the world was made, adopted us, redeemed us, and plans to sum up all things in Christ. Paul prays they will know the hope of God’s calling.
1.d: 1:3–14 is one long, complex sentence in Greek, as Paul’s sentences often are [[tosn:Ephesians 1:3-14]]. The Spirit is God’s pledge of future blessing and a foretaste of eternal life [[tosn:Ephesians 1:14]].

2.s: We were dead in sin, but God made us alive with Christ: “By grace you have been saved through faith… not of works.” Christ has broken down the wall between Jews and Gentiles, making one new people.
2.d: “We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works” [[bible:Ephesians 2:10]]. Good works are the fruit of salvation, not its cause [[tosn:Ephesians 2:10]]; God saves because he is kind and full of grace [[bsn:Ephesians 2:1-10]].

3.s: The mystery revealed to Paul: the Gentiles are fellow heirs. Paul prays that they may know “the width and length and height and depth” of Christ’s love.
3.d: This is Paul’s second prayer for his readers: the first was for understanding, this one for strength and growth [[tosn:Ephesians 3:14-21]]. It ends in a doxology, a statement of praise to God, to “him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think” [[tosn:Ephesians 3:20-21]] [[bible:Ephesians 3:20]].

4.s: Walk worthy of your calling: one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism. Christ gave gifts to equip the church. Put off the old self; speak truth in love; don’t let the sun go down on your anger.
4.d: “When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive” [[bible:Ephesians 4:8]] takes up Psalm 68:18 [[bible:Psalm 68:18]]. This may refer to Christ’s victory over spiritual powers, and he gave gifts to his people (4:11–12) [[tosn:Ephesians 4:8]]. “Be angry, and don’t sin” quotes Psalm 4:4 [[tosn:Ephesians 4:26-27]].

5.s: Be imitators of God; walk in love and light; be filled with the Spirit, singing psalms and hymns. Wives and husbands: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly, and gave himself up for it.”
5.d: All Christians, husbands and wives included, are called to submit to one another out of reverence for Christ [[tosn:Ephesians 5:22]]. Paul reminded the household that God treats no believer as more important than another [[bsn:Ephesians 5:21-6:9]].

6.s: Children and parents, servants and masters. “Put on the whole armor of God”: the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, the shield of faith, the sword of the Spirit.
6.d: “Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood” [[bible:Ephesians 6:12]]. Only with the Lord’s protection can a believer resist the devil [[tosn:Ephesians 6:11]]. The breastplate of righteousness and helmet of salvation recall the Lord himself in Isaiah 59:17 [[bible:Isaiah 59:17]].
